snippet.title: How a Pencil Turned Cheap AMD Chips into Monsters
snippet.description:
In 2000, an ordinary pencil could unlock an AMD Duron. A few graphite marks reconnected the tiny L1 bridges on top of the processor, letting a compatible Socket A motherboard change its clock multiplier. In one test from the time, Tweakers reconnected those bridges and got a 600 MHz Duron to run stably at 900 MHz.

AMD built the Duron to compete with Intel’s Celeron, but early benchmarks showed it could keep up with pricier chips in some games and tests. This video follows what made the Duron so fast for the money, why the early Socket A boards made multiplier control so valuable, and how much the result depended on the individual chip and its cooling.

The trick got harder with the Athlon XP. The Palomino’s laser-cut pits sent overclockers looking for glue and conductive paint, and the mobile Barton later gave them a chip whose multiplier they could change straight from the BIOS. It all started with a budget CPU and four tiny pencil marks.

If you tried the pencil trick back then, what speed did you get?

https://archive.arstechnica.com/reviews/2q00/duron/duron-3.html

https://www.hexus.net/tech/features/cooling/78-amd-duron-overclocking-guide/

https://tweakers.net/reviews/148/amd-duron-overclocking-project.html

https://www.manualslib.com/manual/601758/Abit-Kt7.html

In Today's Episode:
In November 1968, a coal mine outside Farmington, West Virginia exploded with 78 men trapped inside. The company had sealed it shut with them still down there.

Years later, someone found the mine's safety alarm had been rigged so it couldn't go off. That's one chapter in a hundred-year war between the coal companies and the people of Appalachia: armored trains firing on tent camps, private planes dropping bombs on American citizens, a dam of coal waste that erased a whole valley.

Every time, once the bodies were counted, the people responsible went to work making sure the worst of it never got written down.

snippet.title: FLORIDA FLOOD DISASTER WORSENS — I-95 CLOSED, Schools SHUT, More Rain Coming (Latest Updates)
snippet.description:
Florida is flooding again. On Wednesday, November 18, 2026, a multi-day rain event is hammering Florida's Atlantic coast, just two weeks after record flooding turned deadly in Brevard County. Overnight, the National Weather Service estimated 8 to 10 inches of rain fell across parts of Broward County in about three hours, with more than a foot near Hollywood. Parts of I-95 and Florida's Turnpike closed under high water, cars stalled across Hollywood, Davie and Plantation, and Broward County Public Schools closed on Wednesday.

The Weather Prediction Center has the east coast under a rare Moderate Risk (level 3 of 4) of excessive rainfall through Friday, only the second time since 2016 Florida has seen that level in November. Forecasters expect 5 to 10 inches near the coast, with isolated totals of 12 to 20 inches possible in Flagler, Volusia and Brevard counties. Melbourne, which had its rainiest day on record on November 2, is about 8 inches away from its wettest year ever.

The St. Johns River near Cocoa is in major flood stage at 17.13 feet, about five inches below its 1953 record, and river forecasts include only a fraction of the rain still to come. Seminole County officials warn flooding near Lake Harney could last into early December.

Brevard County is still recovering from the October 31 to November 3 flooding, when Malabar measured nearly 29 inches of rain and two men died in Palm Bay. Governor Ron DeSantis has asked President Trump for a major disaster declaration for nine counties, which was unsigned as of Tuesday. In Melbourne, 90 residents of the Windover Palms apartments must leave by Friday after flood damage.

In this video, we cover the overnight flash flooding in Broward County, the rare flood threat for the Space Coast and Volusia County, the rising St. Johns River, the weather pattern behind the repeated storms, emergency preparations in Palm Bay, the push for FEMA aid, and the outlook into the weekend.

AI writes most of your pull requests now, but you're the one clicking merge. CodeRabbit reads every file first and shows you what it breaks. Start a free 14-day CodeRabbit trial with my link. No credit card required: https://ntck.co/coderabbit


Git is the game save for your code. Before I walk into the scary room in Resident Evil, I save on the typewriter, and before your AI agent touches your code, you should too. So we build a tiny repo (a website and a zombie story), then save it, break it, restore it, and jump back in time with the DeLorean. Then we branch off the sacred timeline, put it on GitHub, hand issues to an AI agent, and commit a timeline crime on purpose so you know how to fix it. In this video you'll learn what Git actually is (and why it is not GitHub), how staging, commits, git log and git diff work, how to time travel with git checkout and git restore, how branches and merges work, and how issues, pull requests and merge conflicts let you work alongside an AI agent without wrecking main. Whether you have never typed git init or your agent has been doing it for you this whole time, by the end you'll know Git better than your AI.

RESOURCES / LINKS:
📖 Follow-along guide (every command, step by step): https://github.com/theNetworkChuck/git-guide
🛠️ Download Git: https://git-scm.com/downloads
🛠️ GitHub CLI: https://cli.github.com
🌐 GitHub (free account): https://github.com


GIT COMMANDS (the copy and paste list I promised):
Check if you have Git: git --version
Tell Git who you are: git config --global user.name "Your Name"
git config --global user.email "you@example.com"
Make main the default branch: git config --global init.defaultBranch main
Turn a folder into a repo: git init
What's going on?: git status
Stage your changes: git add .
Save the game: git commit -m "my first commit"
See your save points: git log --oneline
See what changed: git diff (and git diff --staged)
Undo changes to a file: git restore zombiestory.md
Time travel to an old commit: git checkout COMMIT_HASH
Back to the present: git switch main
Make a branch and jump in: git branch zombieattack, then git switch zombieattack
Merge it into main: git switch main, then git merge zombieattack
Delete a branch: git branch -d zombieattack
Log in to GitHub: gh auth login
Make a private repo on GitHub: gh repo create YOUR_REPO --private
Connect your repo to GitHub: git remote add origin YOUR_REPO_URL.git
Push it up: git push -u origin main
Download a repo: git clone YOUR_REPO_URL
Grab the latest: git pull
Grab a branch without merging: git fetch, then git branch -a
Create an issue: gh issue create --title "Add a line" --body "Add one more line to zombiestory.md"
Review and merge a pull request: gh pr checkout 3, then gh pr merge 3 --merge

snippet.title: 🧗🏼 A Mini Climbing Wall Built Into a Crumbling Wall | Made in Cinema 4D by Digital Creator 3d.zhe
snippet.description:
As time erodes our concrete jungles, digital creator 3d.zhe discovers opportunities for 3D creativity hidden within forgotten public spaces.

Using the Creality Pika, a pocket-sized handheld 3D scanner, 3d.zhe captures every chip and jagged edge along the battered corner of a brick building.

Imported into Cinema 4D, that reality capture becomes the blueprint for a custom climbing wall that fits seamlessly into the gap.

Even the holds are pure digital fabrication, shrunk down from a scan of a real one and printed in bright colors. A crew of hand-painted climbers puts them to the test, roped in all the way to the top.

Keep an eye on the cracks. You never know what you'll discover.
